title: The same credential in different OpenTelemetry log record fields
summary: One synthetic GitHub classic personal access token literal is placed, in turn, in the string body of an OTLP/JSON log record, in a map-and-array nested body, in an attribute value, in exception text (message and stack trace), in a resource attribute and inside a body string that holds serialized JSON, while the same record always carries a trace id and a span id. A last record holds two distinct literals and a trace id in upper-case hex.
rationale: The OpenTelemetry data model gives a log record several places for free-form data (Body is any value, so a string or nested maps and arrays; Attributes; the Resource; and, by the exception conventions, exception.message and exception.stacktrace) and classifies none of them as holding secrets or as exempt. The failure mode is deciding by field: treating Body as 'the message' and the attribute collection as 'metadata', treating exception text as diagnostic-only, or reading the sibling members key and value of an OTLP attribute as unrelated, so that a literal credential in one position is missed while the same literal in another is found. The twin and mutation relation is the point: the base value is unchanged between records and only the position changes, so the expectation must not change. Two further facts keep the spans exact. In a body string that holds serialized JSON, the quotes around the value are written as backslash-quote, which belong to the envelope and not to the value. The trace id and span id are the record's own correlation identifiers (hex, case-insensitive in OTLP/JSON); they are neighbours of the credential, not part of it, and must not be absorbed into its span. A literal value alone is not made secret by the carrier, and the carrier alone does not make a value secret: it is the credential's own documented status that does.

expectation.rationale: Each literal token occurrence is a secret wherever the record places it, and its span is the token only. The issuer's page says to treat its access tokens like passwords. The OpenTelemetry pages say what the carrier can hold, not that any field is exempt: Body is any value including nested maps and arrays, exception.message carries a warning that it may contain sensitive information, and the project's own guidance lists authentication credentials and session tokens among sensitive data while saying that what is sensitive varies by situation and that OpenTelemetry cannot decide it. The carrier independence is this Case's reasoning from those statements (the data model assigns no field a protected or exempt status), not a statement by any of the cited pages; a reviewer who reads the data model differently should dispute it. Nothing here says a trace id or span id is or is not confidential: they are expected unflagged as identifiers (the existing spec-defined identifier Case, W3C trace-id) and are not given spans. Decoding preconditions: none for the fixtures here, because the token bytes appear contiguously and unescaped in the source; a token written with JSON unicode escapes, or carried in the base64 of a bytesValue, is a different representation, not asserted here. Whether any consumer parses OTLP/JSON, descends into nested values or decodes a JSON string is that consumer's behaviour and is not assumed.

sources.supports: Treat your access tokens like passwords (a warning that applies to both fine-grained personal access tokens and personal access tokens (classic)).

sources.supports: Body is an AnyValue that can be a free-form string or structured data composed of arrays and maps of other values; Attributes is a collection of AnyValue whose values vary per occurrence; errors and exceptions are recorded in Attributes under the exception conventions.
sources.locator: Field: Body; Field: Attributes; Errors and Exceptions

sources.supports: exception.message is a string that 'may contain sensitive information'; exception.stacktrace is a string attribute.

Telemetry can inadvertently capture sensitive data; authentication credentials and session tokens are listed as examples; what is sensitive varies from situation to situation and OpenTelemetry cannot determine it.
sources.locator: Handling sensitive data; Your responsibility; Sensitive data considerations

sources.supports: In OTLP/JSON, traceId and spanId are case-insensitive hex strings (not base64), object keys are lowerCamelCase field names, and 64-bit integers are decimal strings.
AnyValue holds one of string, bool, int, double, array, key-value list or bytes; ArrayValue and KeyValueList nest AnyValue and KeyValue.
sources.locator: common.proto: message AnyValue, ArrayValue, KeyValueList, KeyValue

sources.supports: A quotation mark and a backslash inside a JSON string are escaped with a backslash, and control characters such as the line feed are escaped (n).
trace-id is a 16-byte identifier shown as 32 hexadecimal characters and propagated to correlate a trace.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored on 2026-10-04 from the cited pages read raw, before any scanner was consulted. Origin: the fixtures are evidence-derived and synthetic-stress constructions of the OTLP/JSON shape, not observed incident logs; no real log was used. Typical exporter output and field order were not observed. Out of scope here: JSON unicode-escaped token characters, bytesValue base64 (see the base64 Scenario), duplicate attribute keys, and the same value occurring twice in one record (the scaffolder needs a unique substring per span); those and any decode, nesting or streaming capability are consumer follow-ups with #150 and credential-eval, never an assumed capability.
